summary: Restricts Bullet Actor COMP body motion with point-to-point, hinge, or slider constraints, either on individual bodies or between matching bodies from two actor sets.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enables or disables this constraint in the simulation

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Point To Point, Hinge, or Slider constraint mode

key_params.name: bodytobody
key_params.note: Creates constraints between Actor 1 and Actor 2 body lists

key_params.name: collisions
key_params.note: Allows or suppresses collisions between constrained bodies

key_params.name: dispcom
key_params.note: Displays the constraint guide in the viewer

key_params.name: actor1
key_params.note: First actor whose bodies are constrained

key_params.name: bodies1
key_params.note: Body IDs from Actor 1 to constrain

key_params.name: pivot1
key_params.note: Constraint pivot point for Actor 1 bodies

key_params.name: sliderrot1
key_params.note: Slider constraint axis rotation for Actor 1 bodies

key_params.name: bodies2
key_params.note: Body IDs from Actor 2 paired with Actor 1 bodies

key_concepts: Constraint COMP restricts Bullet Actor COMP bodies with point-to-point, hinge, or slider constraints.
Body-to-body mode creates one-to-one constraints between Actor 1 and Actor 2 body lists, with unmatched bodies handled explicitly.
Actor body IDs are zero-based and can be inspected with Bullet Solver CHOP.
Point-to-point constraints pin translation around a pivot while still allowing rotation; hinge constraints restrict rotation to a defined axis.
Slider constraints restrict movement or rotation along a configured axis, and collision behavior between constrained bodies is controlled separately.
common_gotchas: Constraint COMP is for Bullet dynamics; it needs Actor COMPs in a Bullet Solver COMP context.
Actor body IDs are zero-based and can be inspected with Bullet Solver CHOP.
Body-to-body mode pairs body lists one-to-one; unmatched Actor 1 bodies become individual constraints and unmatched Actor 2 bodies are ignored.
A point-to-point constraint on a single body removes translational degrees of freedom but still allows rotation.
Hinge constraints require a meaningful hinge axis; slider constraints require careful axis rotation setup.
Collision behavior between constrained bodies is explicit and may need to be disabled for joints that should not fight themselves.
